title: Using `Values` element in a scalar subquery triggers an error

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Describe the bug

We are trying to work around the absence of the `GREATEST()` function in SQL Server using the Table Value Constructor approach described here:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71022/sql-max-of-multiple-columns/6871572#6871572

That is, given a table `t` like this:

pk | i1 | i2 | i3
-- | -- | -- | --
100 | 1 | 2 | 3
200 | 6 | 5 | 4
300 | 7 | 8 | 9

We would like to generate SQL like this:
```sql
SELECT
  t.pk,
  (SELECT max(tvc.v1) FROM (VALUES (t.i1), (t.i2), (t.i3)) AS tvc (v1)) AS max_i 
FROM
  t
```

To get these results:
pk | max_i
-- | --
100 | 3
200 | 6
300 | 9

We are able to construct the appropriate query (see reproducing example), but when we try to compile it we get an error in `visit_values` here:
https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e0bf5ba169975d879c22bc61b1aaf4261ac0559f/lib/sqlalchemy/sql/compiler.py#L4284-L4286

```
TypeError: sqlalchemy.sql.visitors.Visitable._generate_compiler_dispatch.<locals>._compiler_dispatch()
got multiple values for keyword argument 'include_table'
```

Because `kw` contains the entry `{"include_table": True}`.

Editing the SQLAlchemy code to remove the entry from the passed keywords is enough to make the code run and produce the expected output in our case:
```py
kw.pop("include_table", None)
```

But I'm afraid I don't know enough about why `include_table` is being passed through here to know if this only addresses the symptom of a deeper issue. Or indeed, whether we're not constructing the query in the right way.

Thanks!

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.13

N/A

### Operating system

### To Reproduce

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa

table = sa.Table(
    "t",
    sa.MetaData(),
    sa.Column("pk", sa.Integer),
    sa.Column("i1", sa.Integer),
    sa.Column("i2", sa.Integer),
    sa.Column("i3", sa.Integer),
)

table_value_constructor = sa.values(sa.Column("v1", sa.Integer), name="tvc").data(
    [
        (table.c.i1,),
        (table.c.i2,),
        (table.c.i3,),
    ]
)

maximum = sa.select(sa.func.max(table_value_constructor.c.v1))
maximum_subquery = maximum.scalar_subquery()
query = sa.select(table.c.pk, maximum_subquery)

print("-- Select maximum clause")
print(maximum)
print()

print("-- Select maximum clause as scalar subquery")
print(query)
```
